one_line: Gajapati emperor of Odisha who battled Bengal, Vijayanagara, and Golconda while guarding Jagannath’s realm.

appearance.age_look: Late 30s to early 40s, tall and broad-shouldered with a disciplined warrior’s build.
appearance.face: Oval face with a strong jaw, medium–deep brown complexion, sharp nose, neatly trimmed black moustache, a small tilaka line of sandalwood paste on the forehead; default expression calm and composed with steady, serious eyes that hint at both piety and strategic focus.
appearance.hair: Glossy black hair drawn back into a high, tight warrior topknot (kudumi-style) at the back of the crown, sides kept smooth, no loose strands; a simple golden mukuta-band (low crown-band) encircles the head, set with a single central red stone above the tilaka.
appearance.costume: Era-accurate late 15th–early 16th century eastern Indian royal attire: a rich, deep-red silk angavastra-style upper cloth draped over both shoulders and across the chest, secured neatly so it covers the torso and falls to mid-thigh, worn over a finely woven, cream-coloured, short-sleeved cotton tunic; a gold-bordered, dark emerald-green silk dhoti wrapped tightly and brought between the legs in a practical warrior style, tied at the waist and reaching to the ankles; at the waist a broad, engraved gold belt with subtle floral Odia motifs; on his forearms, plain polished steel bracers with small etched patterns; feet in brown leather sandals; jewellery limited to a single medium-length gold necklace with a small round Jagannath pendant, plain gold bangles on each wrist, and small rounded gold earrings; fabrics are smooth silk and cotton, with simple repeating geometric borders in gold at the edges, avoiding overly ornate patterns to keep a martial feel.
appearance.signature: A long, slightly curved Odia steel sword (talwar-type) with a simple cross-guard hilt and a modestly flared disc pommel, worn at his left hip in a plain dark-brown leather scabbard with a subtle golden chape.

ref_desc: Prataparudra Deva is a tall, broad-shouldered, medium–deep brown man in his early 40s with a neat black moustache, black warrior topknot and gold headband, wearing a deep-red silk upper cloth, cream tunic, emerald-green dhoti, gold belt and Odia sword at his left hip.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character model of Prataparudra Deva as a historically grounded early 16th-century Odishan Gajapati king: a tall, broad-shouldered man in his late 30s or early 40s with a medium–deep brown complexion, oval face, strong jaw, sharp nose, and a neat black moustache, a small vertical sandalwood tilaka on his forehead, and calm, serious eyes; his glossy black hair is pulled into a high warrior topknot at the back of the crown, with the sides smooth and no loose strands, encircled by a simple golden mukuta headband set with a single red stone above the tilaka; he wears a rich deep-red silk angavastra-style upper cloth draped securely over both shoulders and across the chest, fully covering the torso and hanging to mid-thigh, over a cream-coloured, short-sleeved cotton tunic, paired with a dark emerald-green silk dhoti wrapped tightly in a practical warrior style, brought between the legs and tied at the waist, reaching to the ankles; a broad engraved gold belt with subtle floral Odia motifs cinches his waist, and he has plain polished steel bracers on his forearms, brown leather sandals on his feet, a medium-length gold necklace with a small round Jagannath pendant, plain gold bangles, and small rounded gold earrings; at his left hip hangs his signature long slightly curved Odia steel sword in a plain dark-brown leather scabbard with a golden chape; colours should be dominated by deep red, emerald green, cream, gold and dark brown, with clean shonen-anime linework and consistent details visible from head to toe.
